page: Amazon Web Services r8i.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized instance powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the platform exposes 96 physical cores and 192 vCPUs operating at clock speeds up to 3.9 GHz, supported by 480 MB of shared L3 cache and advanced instruction set extensions including AVX-512 and AMX. The instance is configured with 1,536 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio. It does not provide bundled local NVMe storage or dedicated GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage via its 75 Gbps baseline network interface.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier execution across multi-threaded and memory-intensive evaluations. The instance attained 209,058.58 points on multi-core stress-ng tests and 145,955.85 on the PassMark CPU suite, driven by its 192 dedicated processing threads and broad vector instruction support. Memory throughput benchmarks show uncached read speeds of 585.17 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 232.99 GB/sec. Application tests highlight top-decile execution for in-memory operations, achieving 296.12 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks, 34,425.01 on PassMark database benchmarks, and 281.14 GB/sec throughput for static web delivery. While single-threaded performance lands in the middle 50% tier, overall compute capacity scales linearly across parallel threads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the bare-metal architecture removes hypervisor virtualization penalties and provides dedicated access to substantial DDR5 memory capacity. Organizations requiring massive in-memory scale benefit from consolidating distributed database clusters into a unified large-memory node. However, the absence of local disks necessitates careful network storage provisioning to prevent remote I/O bottlenecks.

Amazon Web Services r8i.metal-48xl is engineered for enterprise in-memory databases such as SAP HANA or Redis, large-scale Clang compilation jobs, in-memory analytics engines, and CPU-based LLM inference batching.
